notes: Daily Yamamoto-first concert-discovery pass under the current main-branch contracts. Fresh checks covered ALFIE, BODY&SOUL, Space M&A, KEYSTONE CLUB TOKYO and current Yamamoto schedule sources before moving through Tokyo/Kanto and official venue calendars in Washington, Arlington, Alexandria, Bethesda, Baltimore, Philadelphia, Newark/New Jersey and New York. Canonical, active, processed and review artifacts were searched before admission. The surfaced Yamamoto dates and the strongest US-corridor programs were already represented or unchanged. Three October 29 Tokyo announcements are admitted for event-specific reasons: Hiromi revives the Trio Project with James Genus and returning drummer Simon Phillips; Kei Akagi brings his ten-year working trio and two new recordings to its first COTTON CLUB appearance; and Miki Hirose places his own compositions and arrangements inside a thirteen-member jazz orchestra spanning funk, Latin and vocal repertoire. Stage 2 assigns A+ to Hiromi and Akagi and A to Hirose. Scarcity was challenged explicitly: Hiromi follows a sixteen-city tour and plays fourteen Tokyo sets, Akagi's trio has worked together for a decade, and Hirose's orchestra is an active project with two sets. None warrants S or S+. Jazz Momentum 2027 was deferred because the lineup remains TBA beyond music director Shun Ishiwaka; Naoko Terai's recurring Christmas program did not establish a sufficiently specific new live context. This is ordinary concert discovery, not Cultural Discovery.

events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Hiromi The Trio Project featuring James Genus and Simon Phillips from Monday, December 28, 2026 through Sunday, January 3, 2027. December 28 and 29 have 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM sets; December 30 and January 1–3 have 4:00 PM and 7:00 PM sets; December 31 has 7:30 PM and 11:00 PM sets, with the second set carrying the countdown. The venue describes this as a new Trio Project lineup after a sixteen-city US and European tour. Standard music charge is ¥12,000; the December 31 second show is ¥17,000. Member reservations open November 13 and public web reservations November 20.

provenance.note: Stage 1 admission rests on hearing Hiromi reactivate the Trio Project as a new Genus–Phillips rhythm section, not on her fame. Stage 2 assigns A+: the changed bass voice and returning drummer merit actively making room in Tokyo. Fourteen sets and the preceding sixteen-city tour make A+ sufficient; S would inflate scarcity. Repository-wide searches found no matching event, source URL or same-date bill.

en.why_it_matters: This is not simply another Hiromi trio date: James Genus changes the bass center of gravity while Simon Phillips reconnects the new unit to the earlier Trio Project's explosive rhythmic architecture. After a sixteen-city tour, the Tokyo run should reveal a band whose fast reflexes have already been tested in public.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the Tokyo sets, especially if the countdown format appeals. The new lineup is a strong city-level anchor, but fourteen shows and a prior international tour remove any honest claim of one-night scarcity.

es.why_it_matters: No es simplemente otra fecha de trío de Hiromi: James Genus cambia el centro de gravedad del bajo y Simon Phillips conecta la nueva unidad con la arquitectura rítmica explosiva del Trio Project anterior. Después de una gira de dieciséis ciudades, la residencia en Tokio debe mostrar una banda cuyos reflejos ya fueron probados en público.
es.trip_verdict: Le haría espacio activamente a uno de los sets de Tokio, sobre todo si interesa el formato de cuenta regresiva. La nueva formación es un ancla fuerte dentro de la ciudad, pero catorce funciones y una gira internacional previa eliminan cualquier argumento honesto de escasez de una sola noche.

events.subtitle: Backfloating & Midnight Sidewalk — first COTTON CLUB appearance
events.category: Japanese jazz master / working piano trio
events.factual_description: COTTON CLUB presents Kei Akagi Trio's Backfloating & Midnight Sidewalk on Tuesday, January 26, 2027. Doors open at 6:00 PM and the one-show performance with an intermission starts at 7:00 PM. The trio is Kei Akagi on piano, Shunya Wakai on bass and Sota Kira on drums. The venue identifies this as the ten-year working trio's first COTTON CLUB appearance and links the program to its two June 2026 releases, Backfloating and Midnight Sidewalk. Table seating is ¥6,600, with box and pair seating up to ¥9,000. Member reservations open November 5 and public web reservations November 11.

enrichment.note: The primary venue page verifies the date, full trio, ten-year working history, two-album program, charge and authorized reservation path. Exact Apple Music pages for Backfloating or Midnight Sidewalk were not established in the US storefront during this pass.

sources.name: COTTON CLUB
sources.note: Primary venue page confirms the first-appearance context, complete trio, two June recordings, schedule, charges and reservation openings.

provenance.note: Stage 1 admission rests on a ten-year working trio bringing two newly released books into its first COTTON CLUB date; Akagi's Miles Davis history is context, not the admission reason. Stage 2 assigns A+: the ensemble continuity and fresh repertoire merit actively making room. The stable decade-long unit and absence of a premiere, farewell or terminal context keep the event below S. Repository-wide searches found no matching date, bill or source URL.

en.why_it_matters: The draw is the accumulated language of Akagi, Wakai and Kira after ten years as a trio, now carrying two fresh records into the room. Akagi's history matters less here than the chance to hear a settled rhythm section pressure-test a new book in its first COTTON CLUB appearance.
en.trip_verdict: Make room for the January 26 set if Tokyo is in play. A decade-old working trio with current material is a substantial club night, though its continuity argues against treating this venue debut as a singular historical event.

es.why_it_matters: El atractivo está en el lenguaje acumulado por Akagi, Wakai y Kira durante diez años como trío, ahora llevando dos discos recientes a la sala. La historia de Akagi pesa menos aquí que la posibilidad de oír a una sección rítmica asentada poner a prueba un repertorio nuevo en su primera aparición en COTTON CLUB.
es.trip_verdict: Le haría espacio al set del 26 de enero si Tokio ya está en juego. Un trío estable de una década con material actual es una noche de club sustanciosa, aunque esa misma continuidad impide tratar el debut en la sala como un hecho histórico singular.

events.subtitle: Original compositions and arrangements across jazz, funk and Latin grooves
events.category: Japanese jazz orchestra / composer-arranger led ensemble
events.factual_description: COTTON CLUB presents Miki Hirose Jazz Orchestra on Friday, February 5, 2027. The first show opens at 5:00 PM and starts at 6:00 PM; the second opens at 7:45 PM and starts at 8:30 PM. The thirteen-member published lineup includes two trumpets, four saxophones, two trombones, piano, bass, percussion, drums and vocals. The venue says the program centers Hirose's original compositions and arrangements, mixing jazz with funk and Latin grooves; vocal selections are planned from standards through Stevie Wonder and the Beatles. Table seating is ¥7,000 and premium seating reaches ¥9,500. Member reservations open November 5 and public web reservations November 11.

provenance.note: Stage 1 admission rests on Hirose's own writing and arranging for a fully named thirteen-member orchestra that can move between horn mass, Latin percussion, funk rhythm and voice. Stage 2 assigns A: this is worth knowing about and attending if convenient, but the active ensemble, two sets and lack of a premiere or other scarcity fact do not support A+ action language or an S review. Repository-wide searches found no matching event, date or source URL.

en.why_it_matters: Hirose has enough orchestral color to make groove structural rather than decorative: two trumpets, four reeds, two trombones, percussion and drums can move his own writing between brass weight, Latin motion and a vocal front line. The named thirteen-person band is the concrete reason to pay attention.
en.trip_verdict: A worthwhile choice if February 5 fits a Tokyo evening, especially for listeners interested in current Japanese large-ensemble writing. Keep it on the itinerary without displacing a rarer one-off.

es.why_it_matters: Hirose dispone de suficiente color orquestal para que el groove sea estructura y no adorno: dos trompetas, cuatro cañas, dos trombones, percusión y batería pueden mover su propia escritura entre peso de metales, impulso latino y un frente vocal. La banda concreta de trece integrantes es la razón para prestar atención.
es.trip_verdict: Es una opción valiosa si el 5 de febrero encaja en una noche de Tokio, sobre todo para quien siga la escritura actual de grandes ensambles japoneses. La mantendría en el itinerario sin desplazar una ocasión más rara.
